headline: Fossil fuels are millions of years of stored solar energy—ancient deposits we're rapidly spending
universal_truth: Inherited wealth can be spent quickly; know whether you're drawing from income or savings
fun_facts: A gallon of gasoline contains about 500 hours of human labor equivalent in energy
We burn about 1 million years of accumulated fossil fuel deposits every year
Fossil fuels powered the industrial revolution—essentially unlocking an inheritance
discussion_questions: What 'inherited energy' are you spending—from past generations, past work, past investments?
How do you distinguish between income and savings in your resources?
What deposits have you built versus depleted?

hook.script: Oil is concentrated ancient sunlight. Millions of years of photosynthesis, compressed and stored. When you burn gasoline, you're releasing solar energy captured before dinosaurs existed. We inherited an incredible energy savings account—and we're burning through it fast.

cliff.script: Fossil fuels are essentially an inheritance—stored wealth from the past. This framing reveals something important. What does it teach?

options.text: Fossil fuels are savings, not income—we're spending an inheritance built over millions of years; distinguishing stored wealth from flow income is crucial for sustainability
options.response: Yes. Living on inheritance feels great—until it runs out. Fossil fuels let us borrow from the past, but there's a fixed amount. Know when you're spending savings versus earning income.
Energy sources, yes, but the distinction between stored reserves and renewable flow matters...

fact1.title: Savings vs Income
fact1.script: Fossil fuels are savings—accumulated over eons. Renewables are income—flowing continuously. Living on savings works until they're gone. Transition to income is essential for long-term viability.

fact2.title: Incredible Density
fact2.script: One gallon of gasoline equals weeks of human labor. Fossil fuels concentrated enormous energy into convenient packages. This inheritance enabled modern civilization. But inheritance is finite.

fact3.title: Personal Inheritance
fact3.script: What inherited resources are you spending? Skills from education, capital from past work, relationships built over years? These are savings. Know when you're drawing down versus replenishing.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Inherited wealth can be spent quickly. Know whether you're drawing from income or savings. Build reserves, don't just deplete them.

outro.script: That's Day 276. Tomorrow, we'll explore power from splitting atoms—nuclear energy. Until then, consider what inherited resources you're spending.

growTrack.title: Savings vs Income Check - What Are You Depleting?
growTrack.learning_objective: Distinguish stored resources from renewable flows
growTrack.activity: What are your 'fossil fuels'—accumulated resources you're spending? Savings, health, goodwill, reputation built over years? Are you also building new deposits, or just depleting? Balance inheritance spending with income earning.
